message:
feat(task-063): DIRECT_LINK on the access slot authors an open gate

add-recipient accepts auth.access_method DIRECT_LINK (and a one-item list) on
the access slot and maps it to AccessGate::open(), so the domain keeps one
value for an open gate (ADR-0082). In a longer list or on the signing slot it
is still refused. Existing acceptance bodies now send it explicitly; behaviour
is unchanged and the touched tests pass.

feat(task-063): an add-recipient with no access declaration is a 422

An open door said by omission could not be told from a gate a client dropped
by mistake, so a missing declaration is now refused at auth.access_methods.
The dashboard handoff documents the breaking change with before/after bodies,
and ADR-0082 lands as Proposed with its index, graph and crosswalk entries.

feat(task-064): the trail states the access gate a claim was made under

RecipientClaimed now records access_gate_was_open, so a declaration changed
after the claim no longer rewrites what the trail says about it. The machine
code-send and relayed-answer routes record the opening before opening a
session, and the trail lists each change of a party's gates under that party.

docs(task-063): the published contract says the access gate is always declared

OpenAPI strings and docblocks no longer describe an open gate as said by
omission, and the signing list is described as optional and refusing
DIRECT_LINK. ADR-0082 records that it amends ADR-0077 section 2.9.

feat(task-064): the envelope replaces a recipient's gates until they first open their link

Envelope::changeRecipientAuthRequirement() replaces both gates while the
envelope is open and the recipient has not entered. The declared-method
availability check that add-recipient used moves into a shared service so both
paths apply the same rule.

docs(task-063): ADR-0082 is accepted and names the tests that realize it

TASK-063 realizes every clause of section 2. The ADR now lists the landed
tests and symbols, and the add-recipient access rule has its mutation-test
survivors pinned (refusal messages quoted by the handoff, unknown signs_via).

Merge feat/explicit-access-gate: TASK-063, the access gate is always declared

An add-recipient with no access declaration is now a 422, and an open door is written DIRECT_LINK (ADR-0082).

feat(task-064): a recipient's gates are replaced on the bus under the envelope's lock

ChangeRecipientAuthRequirement loads the envelope with a row lock before
replacing the gates. When the opening's lock is not taken in time, both
machine twins propagate the 503 ENVELOPE_BUSY and open nothing.

Merge develop into feat/gates-editable-before-entry: brings TASK-063

AddRecipientUseCase conflicted over the availability guard; kept the move into DeclaredMethodAvailability with develop's docblock edit.

feat(task-064): PUT .../recipients/{recipientId}/auth replaces a recipient's gates

The machine route takes add-recipient's auth object and access_code. The
wire-to-domain translation moves into one AuthRequirementTranslator shared by
both controllers, an unknown recipient is answered after the envelope's own
refusals, and the shared schema scopes add-recipient's exemptions to that route.

test(task-064): the gate change's refusals and stories hold over HTTP

Every refusal of PUT .../auth answers its code and records no change fact.
The published 422 list takes the method-list cap from its constant, and the
shared auth schema says what an omitted selection means on each route and
cites ADR-0083 section 2.2 for the frozen mode.

docs(task-064): ADR-0083 lands complete, and the docs say gates are editable until entry

ADR-0083 names the tests and classes TASK-064 landed. The classes the change
governs cite it, and the domain models, backlog and handoff state that a
recipient's gates are editable until they first open their link.

docs(task-064): the record states what landed, and the gate-change refusals are pinned

The task record names the branch, the suite that covered it and where each
deferral lives. The route description says a first machine authentication call
also fixes the gates, and the refusal mappings are asserted message by message
after mutation testing found survivors.

Merge feat/gates-editable-before-entry: TASK-064, gates are editable until entry

PUT /api/v1/envelopes/{id}/recipients/{recipientId}/auth replaces a recipient's two gates until their first opening (ADR-0083).

feat(task-066): the resend interval is kept per channel

last_resent_at is split into email_last_resent_at and sms_last_resent_at. A
sender who resends by EMAIL and then SMS is no longer refused the second call
by a single per-recipient clock, and the row lock keeps concurrent resends on
one channel from both passing. Route descriptions and living docs follow.

feat(task-065): each supplied contact is classified as added, changed or unchanged

ADR-0084 decides how the correction route treats each contact under the row
lock: a change is one correction, an addition is its own fact, and re-invites
go only on the channel the contact belongs to. Adds ContactKind, ContactRevision,
narrowed channel resolution, and contacts_changed/contacts_added/revokes on
RecipientCorrected (kinds only, never values).

docs(task-066): resend stamps say a resend may have gone out

An unnamed IN_ORDER resend also stamps the fall-back channel, which usually
sends nothing, so the docs and the migration docblock say "may have gone out".
A test pins that the latest refusing deadline wins when the last channel
checked refuses earlier.

feat(task-065): the trail blanks only the destinations a correction changed

A destination is CORRECTED_AFTERWARDS only when a later correction names that
kind of contact, and each addition is stated under its party. The route
description, the dashboard handoff and ADR-0057 (RecipientCorrected now has
eight keys) describe the classification, the budget and the channels re-sent.

test(fixtures): tests seeded at a fixed date pin the database clock to it

Acts are admitted at the database clock, not at the instant a fixture was
seeded with, so ten Integration tests expired with the calendar. They now pin
the clock to their seed date.

feat(task-065): a correction body records a correction, an addition or nothing

The aggregate classifies each body against the stored contacts (ADR-0084).
A changed contact spends one of the correction budget, an addition spends
nothing, and an unchanged body records nothing. Revocation happens only on a
declared channel's changed contact. The route docs and handoff no longer
promise that declaring a channel re-invites.

Merge fix/fixture-expiry-date-bomb: tests seeded at a fixed date pin the database clock

Ten Integration tests went red with ENVELOPE_EXPIRED once the calendar passed their seed date; a census now keeps new ones from doing the same.

feat(task-065): a correction re-invites only on the channels whose contact it touched

Changing the email of a recipient who declared only SMS used to re-send the
SMS. The re-invitation now follows the changed contact and cancels earlier
invitations only when the correction revokes. The use case's classification
from the locked load is covered by tests.

feat(task-065): an added contact re-invites on that contact's declared channel, once

An addition recorded RecipientContactAdded and nothing reacted to it.
OnRecipientContactAdded now dispatches the re-invitation for that channel only,
and the one-resolution census runs it as one more notification site.

docs(task-067): ADR-0085, recorded values are form fields locked by each signature

Values become read-only AcroForm fields filled before each signature, and
DSS signs into a signature field of ours. PageBox converts a placement on the
displayed page (CropBox, /Rotate) into the widget rectangle in PDF user space.

test(task-065): over HTTP, corrections, additions and no-ops behave as classified

An addition spends nothing, an unchanged body does nothing, and an addition
keeps every refusal except the budget. Landlines and foreign mobiles are
refused as real additions, and the link and re-invitation follow the declared
channel end to end.
Merge develop: the fixture-expiry date-bomb fix
Merge develop into feat/resend-interval-per-channel

feat(task-067): field text follows the signer's layout rules, cut with an ellipsis

Ports the signer app's layout (Helvetica widths, 10 pt down to 7 pt, 3 pt
padding, greedy wrap) with its golden cases. A signature can now name our
signature field, in which case DSS is sent the field instead of coordinates,
and a recipient's reservations are recorded when their commit is admitted.

test(task-066): classify the per-channel migration test in the fixed-date census

Its fixed instants are resend stamps written as given and it admits no act.

Merge feat/resend-interval-per-channel: TASK-066, the resend interval counts per channel

A recipient declared [EMAIL, SMS] can be resent by email and then at once by SMS; the 60-second interval is kept per channel.
Merge develop: TASK-066, the resend interval counts per channel

build(task-067): the image carries pyHanko 0.29.0, pinned by hash, in /opt/pyhanko

A new pyhanko stage builds a venv from a hash-pinned requirements file. A live
DSS test signs into a hand-built PDF whose signature field locks a read-only
text field, and checks the rect and lock survive.

feat(task-067): a PDF's form is read and written by a sealed-off pyHanko process

Adds PdfFormEngineInterface and PyHankoFormEngine, which runs the form engine
script in a separate process. SignRequest documents its optional fieldId, and a
null reservations column at completion also means a commit that carried none.

feat(task-067): a drawn revision is checked before signing and planned from the envelope

DrawnRevisionCheck refuses a revision that does not keep the input bytes or
omits a requested value or lock, naming the failed check. FormRevisionPlanner
decides what one signature's revision creates, fills and locks. The
preparability test states the PAdES rule it rests on.

feat(task-067): the form engine script reads a PDF's form and prepares its fields

form_engine.py implements the protocol's inspect operation and the create and
signatureFields half of apply: one read-only parent field per value and locked
signature fields.

feat(task-067): every signature goes into a field of ours, after a fill revision

DocumentSigner inspects the tip before the first signature of an act and, for
a preparable document, appends one incremental revision planned from the
envelope read. The engine's apply fills each value with the appearance PHP laid
out and never fills a field that is already drawn.
Merge develop into feat/field-values-drawn-into-the-pdf: TASK-066, fixture clock pin

docs(task-065): prose and citations say what a correction does since ADR-0084

ADR-0072 no longer blanks every destination after any correction, and two
notes stop saying a correction returns the recipient to PENDING. Dropping a
declared channel after an invitation revokes, so a correction reads the current
declaration; the route and handoff say so.

fix(task-067): the form engine draws every appearance with its own WinAnsi Helvetica

A document's own /DR /Helv with a /Differences encoding drew other glyphs for
the bytes we write (the ellipsis, for one), and a backslash in a value is now
escaped where it is drawn. New tests seal a single-seal envelope against the
live DSS and use a well-formed sample PDF that pyHanko can read.

test(task-067): each signature locks the values of its own revision, against live DSS

The form reader handles signed PDFs (a signature dictionary's FieldMDP
reference used to recurse forever). Covers SEQUENTIAL_PADES with two signers
and an approver, and a delivery-bar envelope over rotated and offset-CropBox
documents that signs, seals and issues a trail failing no check.

docs(task-067): a PDF the form engine cannot read is signed without drawing

A hand-written fixture with a broken cross-reference table showed the case:
DSS reconstructs it and signs, pyHanko cannot open it. The delivery bar now
asserts the values each signature covers, and mark tests compare rects
numerically since our field writes them.

fix(task-065): dropping a declared channel after an invitation retires its links

A sender who re-declared ["EMAIL"] after the SMS link went to a wrong phone
left that holder a live link. The revocation condition is a link that may have
been minted, which includes an invitation still in flight; the route
description, docblocks and handoff say so.

docs(task-065): the record states what landed, and ADR-0084 is realized

The record lists decisions, unproven properties and debt, the domain models
describe a correction that reaches only the contact it changed, and the
channel-change route keeps its open-leg condition. Fifteen mutation survivors
on the branch's changed lines are now pinned.

fix(task-067): a visible mark signed into our field is drawn at the field's size

DSS 6.4 kept our field's rect but sized an image-above-name mark to its own
content, so viewers squashed it. The request now carries width and height. A
PDF the engine cannot read is signed without drawing and logged with its reason.

docs(task-067): ADR-0085 is indexed, and the docs describe values drawn before signing

Adds the index row and graph edges, names the realizing tests and classes, and
updates the Signature Execution model and the placement and reservations
docblocks. Mark tests on rotated and cropped pages compare the widget BBox with
the field's size.

fix(task-067): recorded values and PDF bytes stay out of exception traces

FormEngineFailedException and the signing act's rethrows carried frames whose
arguments held every field value and the document bytes. They are now kept
out of traces. ADR-0034 and ADR-0023 point at the fill revision ADR-0085 adds.

Merge feat/correction-reaches-the-changed-contact: TASK-065, corrections

The correction route classifies each contact against the stored one under the row lock; an addition spends nothing and re-invites on its own channel (ADR-0084).

fix(task-067): the form engine runs isolated and a drawn revision changes nothing else

The interpreter starts with -I. The new UNTOUCHED check refuses a revision in
which a field changed that was not asked for. A page whose /Rotate is not a
multiple of 90, or whose CropBox lies outside the MediaBox, is signed without
drawing.

fix(task-067): a page no placement fits is signed without drawing

PageBox used to refuse such a page and the adapter turned that into a retry
that could never succeed. The UNTOUCHED check also refuses a summary missing a
signature field that was there before the revision. ADR-0085 and the model
name the hardening.

test(task-067): pin the PageBox geometry, the text layout bounds and the hardening

Infection left 25 PageBox and 25 FieldTextLayout mutants alive, so corner,
boundary and Helvetica width cases are added. The drawing log test now covers
every not-preparable reason, and ADR-0085 and a handoff say the signed PDF
carries the recorded values.

test(task-067): the planner, the output check and the engine adapter are pinned

Mutation testing on the changed lines found them unpinned. Every malformed
engine response is refused and a request or process that cannot start fails by
kind. A multiline cut also drops a max(1, ...) floor that could never apply.

Merge develop into feat/field-values-drawn-into-the-pdf: TASK-065

Conflicts were in the backlog and the ADR index only.

Merge feat/field-values-drawn-into-the-pdf: TASK-067, field values are drawn into the PDF

Before every signature in both signing modes, the recorded values are drawn as read-only AcroForm fields in one incremental revision, and DSS signs into a signature field of ours (ADR-0085).

docs(task-047): each recipient who acts receives a sealed receipt of their own act

The task was a stub blocked on the audit trail, which is now on develop. It
is re-cut to one receipt per signer, approver or decliner. ADR-0072, ADR-0070,
ADR-0073 and TASK-045 stop describing a per-signer evidence document and
point at the receipt.

docs(task-069): a document is sealed as soon as nobody can still sign it

Until now a recipient whose part ended got nothing final until every other
party acted, because the company seal was one act at the envelope's close.
The task proposes sealing each document once its chain is final and the
agreement is secured.

feat(task-070): a recipient reads their copy through a read-only link while it is kept

The signing token expires after 7 days, so a recipient whose part ended could
not get their copy back. COPY_LINK is a registered credential kind, Authn has
the two copy cases, and CopyReadCredentialCodec mints the 15-minute JWT (ADR-0088).
The copy gate lock's wait doubles, and a delegated recipient may hold a link.

feat(task-069): DOCUMENT_READY_TO_SEAL and DOCUMENT_SEALED exist on the wire

Both are declared Contract events with closed key sets. A chain that holds a
seal refuses a further signature or a second seal by name, and
RecipientOutcome::blocksAnEarlySeal() says per outcome whether a recipient still
keeps a document from being sealed early (ADR-0087).

docs(task-047): the session receipt route keys "has acted" on the session's own state

Under SEQUENTIAL_PADES Envelope records completion only on RECIPIENT_SIGNED,
the receipt's own trigger, so a route keyed on Envelope would answer too late.

fix(task-068): an admitted commit reads COMPLETED before its signature lands

The session read and the auth descriptor answered from the landed outcome, so
a signer whose commit was admitted still read AUTH_PASSED. A test replays the
report over HTTP, and ADR-0090 lands as Proposed: after the commit a recipient
is served only a copy that carries their act.

docs(task-071): a recipient is told when their part ends, with their copy

Today nobody hears anything at their own ending, and a signer gets
ENVELOPE_COMPLETED with no link only when the whole envelope ends.

feat(task-068): SignedCopy says where a recipient's copy stands

One Session enum holds the rule for signed_copy, used by the session read, the
download and the commit's 200. After an admitted commit the download serves all
of the recipient's documents or none, and the published summaries say what is
served before and after.

feat(task-070): a copy access record holds its own gate; its lock's wait doubles to a day

CopyAccess is the copy's own gate, one per tenant, envelope and recipient,
issuing delivered-code challenges. The copy surface reads the recipient's
context once through CopyRecipientContextReader, refusing only an unsent
envelope, and Authn documents who the human is for every case.

feat(task-069): the document view names the execution that sealed it

A document can be sealed early by its own execution or by the envelope seal,
so DocumentView gains sealedBy. An early-sealed document waits in staging until
completion and is promoted once, and the promotion read waits for completed_at.

docs(task-069): the sealed-document route says a seal can precede completion

The OpenAPI description and controller docblocks no longer say the route
404s until the envelope completes, and say that only a document carrying a
signature is sealed early. A regression test confirms informational members
still get SEALED_COPY_READY once at completion.

feat(task-070): who may be minted a copy link is one total function

CopyLinkEligibility answers null or a CopyLinkRefusal from standing and
outcome. A copy access challenge now opens only for a delivered method, and the
copy read credential's typ, aud and claim types are each pinned on their own.

feat(task-068): the commit's 200 carries signed_copy, never ready at the commit

The signer frontend stores the commit's answer as its read, so it now says
whether the copy is APPLYING or AWAITING_ENVELOPE. SEAL_PENDING pre-empts
signed_copy only while a readable document is unsealed, and a test checks the
two readers agree for every mode, role and envelope state.

feat(task-047): the receipt is a model of its own with a closed published JSON

A receipt states one recipient and the sending organisation and no other
participant, so it is its own model in Evidence & Audit (Domain/Receipt),
separate from the trail.

feat(event-log): a settled read can stop at the first fact of a type about one subject

An envelope's stream holds one RECIPIENT_SIGNED per recipient, so a type alone
cannot name one recipient's act. read_settled_stream() gains an overload taking
the subject, and the earlier migration's docblock stops calling it the only read.

feat(task-070): copy links are checked at every use; copy access is stored per tenant

CopyAdmission refuses past the conservation ceiling, on a ceiling error or
once retired. session.copy_access and its challenge and attempt tables sit
beside the signing session's, locked per recipient.

feat(task-069): the envelope seal seals only what no other execution sealed

The envelope seal first looks for its own seal on each document, so a
sequential redelivery ends at that check. SealDocument seals one document
early, once, and records DOCUMENT_SEALED. The audit trail holds an early seal
by that fact (ADR-0087).

fix(task-068): the commit's 200 says what each later answer is

It claimed status COMPLETED from now on for both routes, but the session read
refuses with 409 SEAL_PENDING only while the envelope is closed and a visible
document is unsealed. The download's guarantee also names the admitted-commit
axis its test now drives.

feat(task-069): the envelope requests the seal of each document once it is final

Under SEQUENTIAL_PADES a document whose signers have all landed, declined or
been released is sealed once the agreement is secured and while the envelope
is open. OnDocumentReadyToSeal derives the execution id from envelope and
document, and the trail renderer labels both new facts.

feat(task-047): a receipt's sources are gathered up to the recipient's own act

The gatherer reads the stream up to the first fact of the trigger's type about
its subject. The model, not the gathering, is what keeps other participants out.

test(task-069): early sealing over HTTP, under retry and in a race

A seal DSS refuses is retried four times then parked naming the failure. The
waybill with one document per consignee is served each sealed document at the
signature, and the deadline seals only what is left. An early seal racing the
envelope seal leaves one seal either way. isFinal() drops a clause that could
never decide.

feat(task-070): a copy read credential lists and serves what the signing reader would

Copy readers go through CopyAdmission and serve nothing to a decliner. Copy
links are stored as digests behind two definer functions and resolve only by
digest, and copy access child tables now cascade on their parent's deletion.

test(task-068): over HTTP the signer's copy is applied, awaited or final until the seal

A recipient whose commit was admitted meets no 409 on the session read except
SEAL_PENDING, since the signer app would otherwise strand them on its waiting
screen. The census of session reader refusals now sees every way to throw one.

feat(task-070): opening a copy link admits it and sends the access code on the copy record

A link is admitted by CopyAdmission and answered with the recipient's gate
facts without the signing gate's rules. The code is issued and re-sent on the
copy access record, charged to its own budget, while the terminal signing
session stays untouched.

feat(task-047): one receipt record per envelope and recipient, tenant-isolated

evidence_audit.issued_receipt follows issued_trail: row-level security enabled
and forced under the tenant policy.

feat(task-070): answering the copy gate passes it on the copy record

SubmitCopyAuthUseCase admits the link, refuses an open gate or undeclared
method, and answers on the copy record. A code continues on a live method only
while the gate still declares it, and a test pins that session.copy_link has
the digest policy and no other.

feat(task-047): a receipt is assembled from its sources, for its recipient only

ReceiptAssembler builds one recipient's receipt from the stream up to their
act, reading the envelope's title and first close from that prefix.

docs(task-069): the records say a document can be sealed before its envelope closes

LOAD-BEARING still said SealDocument was dispatched by nothing on purpose,
which is no longer true after the early seal. Docblocks name the envelope seal
apart from a document's early seal, and the seal race test is listed in the
PHPStan config like its siblings.

feat(task-070): copy credentials are verified only on the routes that declare them

CopyLinkListener acts only on COPY_LINK: it parses the bearer, resolves its
digest and scopes the request to the link's tenant. The session listeners'
docblocks stop counting their siblings.

feat(task-047): Session answers one recipient's session status through its contract

Evidence & Audit's session route has to know whether the recipient's own act
closed their session, and Session's contract had no such read.
SessionStatusReader adds it. Four untested branches of the receipt's revision
reading are covered.

feat(task-047): a receipt renders as PDF/A-3a with its JSON attached

The receipt is the second document Evidence & Audit issues, so it gets its own
ReceiptRenderer port and Typst adapter over receipt.typ.

docs(task-068): the record states status and debt, and ADR-0090 is accepted

BL-462 closes and BL-267 narrows. The signing-session model carries a dated
banner on COMPLETED, and the download's prose says every readable document is
served once the copy is ready. The owner accepted ADR-0090 on 2026-10-23.

feat(task-047): who gets a receipt, and on which fact, is decided by two exhaustive rules

Signers and approvers get one; the other five roles do not. An approver's
receipt now states their approval, not a signature, and render failures name
the receipt instead of the trail.

feat(task-070): a copy link opens, passes its access gate and earns a read credential

POST /api/v1/copy/open, /copy/auth/otp/send and /copy/auth declare COPY_LINK
and no other route does. The open mints the 15-minute read credential only
when the gate is open or passed. The route docs say where a no-method send goes.

feat(task-047): one recipient's receipt is issued once, when its fact makes it true

IssueReceipt owns its unit of work and mirrors the trail's issuance for one
recipient. Every refusal path is pinned to its retry outlook, and a refusal
reached before the seal is checked to seal nothing.

test(task-068): the commit's 200 body and its schema are each pinned

The HTTP flows for POST /api/v1/signing/commit credit no coverage to the
controller, so mutation testing could not see it; dedicated tests now pin the
body and the published schema. The handoff and model name ADR-0090 as accepted.

feat(task-070): a copy read credential lists and downloads its recipient's documents

GET /api/v1/copy and GET /api/v1/copy/documents/{documentId} run on the copy
read credential. The list description drops the unsent-envelope case, which is
answered 401 before anything is listed.

docs(task-069): an early seal is requested on a signature or once the agreement is secured

A decline or a release alone requests no early seal, and the early seal is
keyed on its own execution. The published sealed-document description and the
related docblocks no longer claim otherwise.

Merge fix/signed-copy-after-commit: TASK-068, the signer is told where their copy stands

From the admission of a commit, GET /api/v1/signing/session answers COMPLETED with a signed_copy member (ADR-0090).

feat(task-047): the fact that ends a recipient's act asks for their receipt

Three reactors translate RECIPIENT_SIGNED, SESSION_COMPLETED and
SESSION_DECLINED into IssueReceipt. A test shows that of two issuances of one
receipt, the one that loses the claim withdraws its custody.

feat(task-070): an integrator mints a copy link through the guarded service

CopyLinkIssuer is the port every caller mints through; its implementation
refuses by the eligibility rule and works for the caller's own tenant's
recipients only. A mint for another tenant is refused, since the read and the
write used different tenant scopes.

feat(task-047): the integrator downloads a recipient's sealed receipt

GET /api/v1/envelopes/{id}/recipients/{recipientId}/receipt on a machine key
serves the receipt with a strong ETag and 304 on a match. An unknown pair or
another tenant's receipt is a 404, each tested after a successful download.

Merge develop into feat/early-document-seal: TASK-068

Brings the signer's signed_copy (ADR-0090); both conflicts were prose in the ADR index and the session read's SEAL_PENDING description.

Merge develop into feat/copy-link: TASK-068, the signer is told where their copy stands

Conflicts were in docs only: the backlog row and the ADR index keep both ADR-0088 and ADR-0090.

feat(task-047): a receipt is kept as long as its envelope once the envelope has ended

app:evidence-audit:conserve-trails now conserves issued receipts too, using a
SECURITY DEFINER funnel that names the tenants holding an unconserved receipt.
The funnel is classified in the sentinel-scope census.

feat(task-070): after their commit a copy serves nothing until it carries their act

The list and the download share one predicate that applies the signing
reader's rule from its single home (SignedCopy::of(), ADR-0090).

feat(task-047): a recipient downloads the receipt of their own act with their session

GET /api/v1/signing/session/receipt is declared in evidence_audit.php so
Session gains no dependency on Evidence & Audit. A receipt whose stream is
still being written waits without failing the conserve job, and the route is
pinned to the session credential and its own tenant.
